articles.full_text:
Raids are underway at the residence and properties of granite baron R. Veeramani following allegations of sexual abuse against minors spanning several years. Investigators are probing the crime and tracking a money trail to determine if influential links or payoffs led to an earlier closure report. Along with Veeramani, his associates Mahendra Simhan, Shanti, and former employee Ganeshan have been arrested after objectionable video clips were recovered. The case has also sparked a political confrontation between the DMK and TVK over alleged delays and police lapses in the initial investigation.
Tamil Nadu Power Cuts: Rising Outages Trigger Public Protests, TNEB Review & Supply Scrutiny
Frequent and unannounced power outages across Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, Trichy, and Tirunelveli, have triggered widespread public anger and street protests amid heatwave conditions. Chief Minister Vijay visited the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board headquarters to review power demand, distribution challenges, shortage of over 600 substations, and aging transformers requiring replacement ahead of anticipated demand surges. Meanwhile, demands have emerged for a white paper regarding peak-hour power purchases at high prices and the cancellation of renewable energy licenses, questioning measures taken to meet state power requirements.
LATEST VIDEOS
A political controversy has emerged following reports highlighting fourteen internal objections raised within the Election Commission over ten months. The concerns primarily involve modifications to Form 6 for new voter registration, database centralisation, and electoral roll procedures in West Bengal and Goa. Opposition parties have demanded judicial scrutiny and raised allegations regarding constitutional safeguards, while the ruling party stated the communication demonstrates democratic functioning. The Election Commission rejected claims of internal rift, asserting that differing views and internal notes are standard components of institutional checks and balances under statutory law.
A reported rift within the Election Commission has triggered a political showdown, with the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar step down. DMK chief MK Stalin questioned the Special Intensive Revision exercise, alleging that over one lakh votes were deleted from the Kolathur seat. The party claims that the voter deletions impacted the election outcome, calling the process a conspiracy as opposition parties raise concerns over the conduct of recent polls.
Villagers from five villages in Dholka near Ahmedabad have been protesting for over a month against severe industrial pollution. Residents of Bethawara, Thrasad, Nesta, Paldi, and Ambali accuse nearby factories of dumping chemical-laced waste into local drains, linking it to rising cancer cases and skin infections. Villagers claim that despite appealing for 15 years to local bodies, the Gujarat Pollution Control Board, and the state government, no action has been taken. The protesters plan to escalate their agitation with a Chakka Jam on roads and highways.

articles.title: Vijay visits power utility HQ as outages spark protests across state - The Hans India
articles.full_text:
Chennai: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay visited the state power utility’s headquarters on Anna Salai in Chennai amid mounting complaints of unannounced electricity cuts across the state, where a heatwave has driven up demand.
Outages have been reported in Chennai, Tiruchirappalli, Tirunelveli and other districts. Residents affected by cuts at night have blocked roads and protested outside electricity offices, demanding that the supply be restored and that officials explain the disruptions.
Reports of power cuts lasting up to two hours have also raised concerns in the industrial and agricultural sectors. For households, the loss of electricity during the night has added to the discomfort caused by the heat. The protests have put pressure on the authorities to respond to complaints and prevent further interruptions.
During his visit, CM Vijay asked officials about the complaints received, the reasons for the outages and the steps being taken to restore supply. He also reviewed the state’s electricity generation, the power it has purchased and whether the available supply can meet the increase in demand. The Chief Minister held discussions with Electricity Minister Nirmal Kumar, power utility chairman Arun Rai and Green Energy Corporation managing director Sridhar. The meeting covered ways to strengthen power infrastructure, meet demand and improve the handling of consumer complaints.
CM Vijay later inspected a power station and the state electricity distribution centre. Officials briefed him on electricity generation and demand, as well as the measures taken when supply was interrupted.
He sought details of the response to outages in affected areas. The visit came as public frustration over the cuts spread beyond residential neighbourhoods. Interruptions have affected businesses and farming operations, while residents have taken their complaints directly to electricity offices.
The outages at night have prompted road blockades in some places. The review focused on both immediate complaints and the capacity of the power system to cope with increased consumption. Officials were asked to account for the electricity being generated and purchased and to explain how disruptions were being addressed.
The government has yet to announce, in the information available, a timetable for ending the outages or further measures arising from the Chief Minister’s inspection. For consumers in the affected districts, the pressing question is whether supply will remain steady as the heatwave continues and electricity use stays high. The protests have made the handling of outages a public test of the utility’s response to rising demand.
